title: Space Missions
blurb: Apollo, Hubble, JWST, Voyager and the explorers behind them

questions.question: Who was the first human to walk on the Moon?
questions.fact: Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969, followed minutes later by Buzz Aldrin.

questions.question: Who was the first human to travel into space, in 1961?
questions.fact: Gagarin's Vostok 1 flight orbited Earth once in about 108 minutes.

questions.question: Which space telescope was launched in 1990 aboard Space Shuttle Discovery?
questions.fact: A flaw in Hubble's mirror was famously fixed by astronauts in a 1993 servicing mission.

questions.question: What does ISS stand for?
questions.fact: The ISS orbits Earth about 16 times a day at roughly 28,000 km/h.

questions.question: What was the first artificial satellite, launched in 1957?
questions.fact: Sputnik 1 was a 58 cm metal sphere that broadcast simple radio beeps.

questions.question: Which mission first landed humans on the Moon?
questions.fact: Apollo 8 was the first crewed mission to orbit the Moon, but Apollo 11 made the first landing.

questions.question: The James Webb Space Telescope mainly observes in which kind of light?
questions.fact: Infrared lets JWST see through dust and spot light from the very first galaxies.

questions.question: In which year was the James Webb Space Telescope launched?
questions.fact: JWST lifted off on Christmas Day, 25 December 2021, on an Ariane 5 rocket.

questions.question: Which spacecraft is the farthest human-made object from Earth?
questions.fact: Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 is so far away that its signals take nearly a day to reach us.

questions.question: The 'Golden Record' with sounds and images of Earth was carried by…
questions.fact: The records include greetings in 55 languages and music from many cultures.

questions.question: Which NASA rover landed on Mars in 2021 carrying the Ingenuity helicopter?
questions.fact: Ingenuity became the first aircraft to make a powered, controlled flight on another planet.

questions.question: Which Apollo mission survived an oxygen tank explosion on the way to the Moon?
questions.fact: The crew used the lunar module as a 'lifeboat' and returned safely to Earth.

questions.question: Who was the first woman in space, in 1963?
questions.fact: Tereshkova orbited Earth 48 times aboard Vostok 6.

questions.question: Which probe flew past Pluto in 2015 and revealed its heart-shaped plain?
questions.fact: New Horizons carries some of the ashes of Clyde Tombaugh, who discovered Pluto in 1930.

questions.question: Which planet is NASA's Juno spacecraft studying?
questions.fact: Juno carries three LEGO figures: Galileo, and the Roman gods Jupiter and Juno.

questions.question: The Cassini mission ended in 2017 by deliberately diving into…
questions.fact: The plunge protected moons like Enceladus, which might be habitable, from contamination.

questions.question: Which spacecraft became the first to 'touch' the Sun by flying through its corona?
questions.fact: Parker is also the fastest human-made object ever, reaching about 690,000 km/h.

questions.question: Which company first landed an orbital-class rocket booster back on land, in 2015?
questions.fact: A Falcon 9 first stage touched down at Cape Canaveral on 21 December 2015.

questions.question: The James Webb Space Telescope orbits around which point in space?
questions.fact: L2 is about 1.5 million km from Earth, where JWST's sunshield can keep it extremely cold.

questions.question: Which mission returned samples from asteroid Bennu to Earth in 2023?
questions.fact: Japan's Hayabusa2 returned samples from a different asteroid, Ryugu, in 2020.

questions.question: What did NASA's DART mission do in 2022?
options: Crashed into an asteroid to change its orbit
questions.fact: DART shortened the orbit of the moonlet Dimorphos by about 32 minutes — the first planetary-defence test.
